You are a verification engineer extending the coverage plan of the design
below. The repository, the baseline regression and its coverage holes, the
existing plan items, the cited documents and the formal environment (the
input assumptions) follow.

# Authoring rules

A plan item is one behaviour of the design that the existing regression
(the baseline testbenches) never exercises. Each item becomes a task: an agent
gets the repository, this item's coverage report entry and its one-line
description, and must write a testbench that reaches it. Every item you
propose is checked mechanically; anything that breaks a rule below is
rejected with the reason.

## The bundle

- **Plan entry.** One-line `description` an engineer could act on (what must
  happen, not how to make it happen), a predicted `tier` (T0 easy, T1 medium,
  T2 hard: cycle-exact or narrow window, T3 multi-step), and `sources`.
  The description restates the cover condition in one or two plain sentences
  and names every signal and value the cover checks. It claims nothing the
  cover doesn't check: stimulus details (which word was pending first, the
  prescale you used) belong in the gold, not the description. Every design
  signal name and every sized or hex constant (8'h3C, 0x3C) in the description
  must be read by the cover; this is checked.
- **Cover file.** One module `cov_ITEM` with one cover property labelled
  `ITEM_<short_name>`, and exactly one `bind <design module> cov_ITEM u_cov_ITEM (.*);`.
  Write the literal token `ITEM`; the tool assigns the real ID.
- **Gold testbench.** Top module `tb`. It reaches the behaviour with legitimate
  stimulus through the design's ports only, and checks it.
- **Near-miss testbenches**: at least one per item. Each exercises nearly the
  same path as the gold but misses the cover by the smallest possible margin
  (one cycle early or late, the other value of the deciding bit, one step
  short of the sequence), checks with `$fatal` that it really exercised that
  path, and runs to `$finish` cleanly. Only if no near-miss is meaningful, add
  `near_miss_waiver: <the reason>` to the plan entry instead; every such item
  is reviewed by a person.

## Cover modules: observe only

Covers run inside every future grading run, so they may only observe.

- Allowed: input ports (named like the design's signals, so `.*` connects
  them; internal registers such as `bit_cnt` or `prescale_reg` can be ports
  too), `parameter`/`localparam`, local registers written with non-blocking
  assignments in `always @(posedge clk)` blocks using only `if`/`case`/`begin`,
  `cover property`, and `$past`, `$rose`, `$fell`, `$stable`.
- Not allowed: initial blocks or variable initializers (reset tracking state
  on `rst` instead; simulation starts every variable at 0), blocking or
  continuous assignments, combinational always blocks, loops, any other
  system task or function, hierarchical references, assertions, instances,
  output ports.
- Verilator 5.020 does not support `##` sequences. For multi-step behaviour,
  track progress in local registers and cover the final state.
- Make the cover exact. A cover that is true too easily (e.g. `a |-> b`,
  which holds whenever `a` is low) is hit by the baseline and rejected.
  Where correctness of data matters, require a specific value (e.g. 8'h55)
  so a mistimed run cannot satisfy it by accident.

## Gold testbenches: check, do not only reach

- Check the behaviour's observable outputs and call `$fatal` if they are
  wrong. Write checks as `if (!ok) $fatal(1, "...")`, never `assert`/`assume`:
  the grader compiles without `--assert`, so assertions never fire.
- No `force`/`release`, no hierarchical writes into the design, no `$system`,
  `$c` or file I/O.
- End with `$finish`. A run that times out, ends without `$finish`, or calls
  `$fatal`/`$stop` scores 0.
- Instantiate the design with its default parameters (overrides are rejected);
  covers may rely on the defaults, e.g. DATA_WIDTH = 8.
- Verilator runs `<=` inside initial blocks and tasks as blocking. Drive and
  sample on the falling clock edge to avoid races with the design.

## Sources

Every item cites at least one source; each is verified mechanically.

- `RTL` / `README`: `file` (repository path), `lines: [first, last]`, and an
  `anchor` string that appears verbatim on those lines.
- `DOC`: `doc` (id), `page`, and an `anchor`: a sentence quoted from that page
  as it reads in the document. Spacing does not matter (the PDF text below has
  extraction artefacts such as `TV ALID` or `TheUART`; quote the words
  normally), but letters and punctuation must match, including case. The
  anchor must appear on that page only: if it also appears elsewhere, quote
  more of the sentence. Use only the pages given.
- `BASE`: `point: {kind, file, line, name}`, a baseline coverage hole from the
  list below (0 hits).
- Mark a `DOC` or `README` source `role: requirement` only if it states what
  the design must do. `RTL` describes what the design does, so it is never a
  requirement.

## What makes a good item

- The baseline never exercises it, and it matters: either a bug in the
  design would make the gold fail, or a cited document requires it.
- It is distinct from every existing item and from your other candidates:
  some testbench must be able to hit one and not the other.
- Difficulty comes from the engineering (exact timing, narrow windows, deep
  sequences, combinations), never from vague wording.

```
   9| ## Deprecation Notice
  10| 
  11| This repository is superseded by https://github.com/fpganinja/taxi.  All new features and bug fixes will be applied there, and commercial support is also available.  As a result, this repo is deprecated and will not receive any future maintenance or support.
  12| 
  13| ## Introduction
  14| 
  15| This is a basic UART to AXI Stream IP core, written in Verilog with cocotb
  16| testbenches.
  17| 
  18| ## Documentation
  19| 
  20| The main code for the core exists in the rtl subdirectory.  The uart_rx.v and
  21| uart_tx.v files are the actual implementation, uart.v simply instantiates both
  22| modules and makes a couple of internal connections.
  23| 
  24| The UART transmitter and receiver both use a single transmit or receive pin.
  25| The modules take one parameter, DATA_WIDTH, that specifies the width of both
  26| the data bus and the length of the actual data words communicated.  The
  27| default value is 8 for an 8 bit interface.  The prescale input determines the
  28| data rate - it should be set to Fclk / (baud * 8).  This is an input instead
  29| of a parameter so it can be changed at run time, though it is not buffered
  30| internally so care should be used to avoid corrupt data.  The main interface
  31| to the user design is an AXI4-Stream interface that consists of the tdata,
  32| tvalid, and tready signals.  tready flows in the opposite direction.  tdata
  33| is considered valid when tvalid is high.  The destination will accept data
  34| only when tready is high.  Data is transferred from the source to the
  35| destination only when both tvalid and tready are high, otherwise the bus is
  36| stalled.
  37| 
  38| Both interfaces also present a 'busy' signal that is high when an operation is
  39| taking place.  The receiver also presents overrun error and frame error strobe
  40| outputs.  If the data word currently in the tdata output register is not read
  41| before another word is received, then a single cycle pulse will be emitted
  42| from overrun_error and the word is discarded.  If the receiver does not get a
  43| stop bit of the right level, then a single pulse will be emitted from the
  44| frame_error output and the received word will be discarded.
  45| 
  46| ### Source Files
  47| 
  48|     rtl/uart.v     : Wrapper for complete UART
  49|     rtl/uart_rx.v  : UART receiver implementation
  50|     rtl/uart_tx.v  : UART transmitter implementation

  60|                     _______________________
```

## Baseline testbenches

### designs/uart/baseline/tb_uart_rx.sv
```systemverilog
// Baseline testbench for uart_rx.
//
// Port of the upstream tests (alexforencich/verilog-uart @ 1b867e5):
//   tb/uart_rx/test_uart_rx.py  (cocotb): payload lengths 1..15 and 128,
//                                         incrementing and PRBS31 data
//   tb/test_uart_rx.py          (MyHDL):  two "walk" patterns
// Differences from upstream, on purpose:
//   - prescale = 5 (current upstream value), bits driven at exactly
//     prescale*8 clocks (upstream's cocotb baud was ~4% off the DUT's rate).
//   - cocotbext UartSource / AxiStreamSink replaced by small SV tasks.
// Like upstream, the sink is always ready and every frame is well-formed.
`timescale 1ns / 1ps

module tb_uart_rx;

  localparam int CLK_PERIOD = 8;  // 125 MHz, as upstream
  localparam logic [15:0] PRESCALE = 16'd5;

  logic        clk = 1'b0;
  logic        rst = 1'b0;
  logic        rxd = 1'b1;
  logic        m_axis_tready = 1'b1;
  logic [15:0] prescale = PRESCALE;
  wire  [7:0]  m_axis_tdata;
  wire         m_axis_tvalid;
  wire         busy, overrun_error, frame_error;

  always #(CLK_PERIOD / 2) clk = ~clk;

  uart_rx #(.DATA_WIDTH(8)) dut (
    .clk(clk), .rst(rst),
    .m_axis_tdata(m_axis_tdata), .m_axis_tvalid(m_axis_tvalid),
    .m_axis_tready(m_axis_tready),
    .rxd(rxd),
    .busy(busy), .overrun_error(overrun_error), .frame_error(frame_error),
    .prescale(prescale)
  );

  // ---------------- scoreboard ----------------
  byte unsigned expected[$];
  int unsigned  n_sent = 0, n_recv = 0;

  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (m_axis_tvalid && m_axis_tready) begin
      byte unsigned exp_b;
      if (expected.size() == 0) $fatal(1, "unexpected byte 0x%02h", m_axis_tdata);
      exp_b = expected.pop_front();
      if (m_axis_tdata !== exp_b)
        $fatal(1, "byte %0d: got 0x%02h, expected 0x%02h", n_recv, m_axis_tdata, exp_b);
      n_recv++;
    end
  end

  // ---------------- stimulus helpers ----------------
  // All testbench driving/sampling happens on the falling edge, so DUT inputs
  // are stable at every rising edge (Verilator runs '<=' in initial blocks as
  // '=', so posedge-driven stimulus would race the DUT).
  task automatic wait_clks(input int n);
    repeat (n) @(negedge clk);
  endtask

  task automatic do_reset();
    rst = 1'b0; wait_clks(2);
    rst = 1'b1; wait_clks(2);
    rst = 1'b0; wait_clks(2);
  endtask

  // 8N1 frame on rxd, LSB first, each bit prescale*8 clocks.
```

```systemverilog
// Like upstream, bytes within a payload are sent back-to-back over AXI-Stream.
`timescale 1ns / 1ps

module tb_uart_tx;

  localparam int CLK_PERIOD = 8;  // 125 MHz, as upstream
  localparam logic [15:0] PRESCALE = 16'd5;

  logic        clk = 1'b0;
  logic        rst = 1'b0;
  logic [7:0]  s_axis_tdata = '0;
  logic        s_axis_tvalid = 1'b0;
  logic [15:0] prescale = PRESCALE;
  wire         s_axis_tready;
  wire         txd;
  wire         busy;

  always #(CLK_PERIOD / 2) clk = ~clk;

  uart_tx #(.DATA_WIDTH(8)) dut (
    .clk(clk), .rst(rst),
    .s_axis_tdata(s_axis_tdata), .s_axis_tvalid(s_axis_tvalid),
    .s_axis_tready(s_axis_tready),
    .txd(txd),
    .busy(busy),
    .prescale(prescale)
  );

  // ---------------- line monitor + scoreboard ----------------
  byte unsigned expected[$];
  int unsigned  n_sent = 0, n_recv = 0;

  // All testbench driving/sampling happens on the falling edge, so DUT inputs
  // are stable at every rising edge (Verilator runs '<=' in initial blocks as
  // '=', so posedge-driven stimulus would race the DUT).
  task automatic wait_clks(input int n);
    repeat (n) @(negedge clk);
  endtask

  // Decode 8N1 frames on txd: find the start edge, then sample mid-bit.
  initial begin
    forever begin
      byte unsigned b;
      int bit_clks;
      @(negedge txd);
      bit_clks = int'(prescale) * 8;
      wait_clks(bit_clks / 2);
      if (txd !== 1'b0) $fatal(1, "glitch: start bit not low at mid-bit");
      for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) begin
        wait_clks(bit_clks);
        b[i] = txd;
      end
      wait_clks(bit_clks);
      if (txd !== 1'b1) $fatal(1, "missing stop bit");
      if (expected.size() == 0) $fatal(1, "unexpected byte 0x%02h", b);
      if (b !== expected[0])
        $fatal(1, "byte %0d: got 0x%02h, expected 0x%02h", n_recv, b, expected[0]);
      void'(expected.pop_front());
      n_recv++;
    end
  end

  // ---------------- stimulus helpers ----------------
  task automatic do_reset();
    rst = 1'b0; wait_clks(2);
    rst = 1'b1; wait_clks(2);
    rst = 1'b0; wait_clks(2);
  endtask

  // AXI-Stream transfer: hold tdata/tvalid until a clock edge with tready high.
  // Leaves tvalid asserted so the next byte follows back-to-back.
  task automatic axis_send(input byte unsigned b);
    bit ready;
    s_axis_tdata  = b;
    s_axis_tvalid = 1'b1;

    // one rising edge pass. If it was high, the transfer happened on that edge.
    do begin
      ready = s_axis_tready;
      @(negedge clk);
    end while (!ready);

    n_sent++;
  endtask

    foreach (data[i]) axis_send(data[i]);
```

- R1 (R1_frame_error): The receiver flags a frame error: a frame ends with the stop bit low, so frame_error pulses and the word is discarded.
- R2 (R2_false_start_rejected): A start bit is rejected as false. At the mid-start-bit sample (prescale_reg == 0 and bit_cnt == 10) the synchronised input rxd_reg is already high again, so the receiver abandons the frame.
- R3 (R3_overrun_second_word): While m_axis_tvalid is high holding 8'h3C and m_axis_tready is low, a second good frame completes. At that point overrun_error is high, m_axis_tvalid is still high and m_axis_tdata has changed to 8'hA5.
- R4 (R4_rx_backpressure_hold): On uart_rx, m_axis_tvalid stays high with m_axis_tready low for at least four consecutive cycles, m_axis_tdata does not change and overrun_error stays low throughout. On the first cycle m_axis_tready is high the word is accepted with m_axis_tvalid high, m_axis_tdata equal to 8'hA5 and overrun_error low.
- R5 (R5_rst_mid_frame_pending): rst is asserted while busy and m_axis_tvalid are both high. After rst is released with m_axis_tvalid and busy low, the receiver later presents a new word with m_axis_tvalid high and m_axis_tdata equal to 8'hA5.
- T1 (T1_tx_reset_mid_frame_low): While the transmitter is busy (busy is 1) and txd is low, rst is sampled high. On the next clock txd is 1 (mark) and busy is 0.
- R6 (R6_break_repeated_frame_error): While rxd is held low continuously, frame_error pulses a second time with rxd low at every clock since the previous frame_error pulse. At that second pulse m_axis_tvalid is low.
- R7 (R7_rx_max_prescale): With prescale held at 16'hFFFF, the receiver's prescale_reg must be loaded with the full, untruncated 19-bit bit-period reload 19'h7FFF7. After that, m_axis_tvalid must rise with m_axis_tdata == 8'hA5.
- T2 (T2_tx_max_prescale_5a): With prescale held at 16'hFFFF, uart_tx accepts a byte and shifts it out on txd. Sampled at the eight data-bit boundaries, txd forms 8'h5A. On the cycle after the last data bit, prescale_reg is 19'h7FFF8, bit_cnt is 0 and txd is high (stop bit).
- R8 (R8_reset_midframe_clears_outputs): While the receiver is busy (busy 1) on a new frame and still holds an already handed-off word (m_axis_tdata 8'hA5, m_axis_tvalid 0), rst is sampled high. On the next clock, with rst still high, busy is 0, m_axis_tvalid is 0 and m_axis_tdata is 8'h00.
- R9 (R9_rx_reset_mid_frame_prompt_restart): While the receiver is mid-bit (prescale_reg above 19'd16), rst is first sampled high with rxd low. rxd then stays low through the reset and after its release, busy is low on the first two clocks after rst falls, and busy is high on the third.
- R10 (R10_rst_clears_frame_error): rst is sampled high on a clock where frame_error is high. On the next clock rst is still high and frame_error is low, so reset clears the frame-error strobe.
- R11 (R11_rst_clears_overrun): While overrun_error is high, rst is sampled high on that same clock; on the next clock rst is still high and overrun_error is low, so reset clears the overrun strobe.
- T3 (T3_tready_low_through_held_reset): With the idle transmitter showing s_axis_tready high, rst is sampled high on three consecutive clocks. s_axis_tready is 0 on the second and third of those clocks, so it stays low for the whole held reset.
- T4 (T4_tx_reset_mid_frame_ready_timing): rst is sampled high while the transmitter's prescale_reg is above 19'd16 (reset in the middle of a bit).   input wire        rst,
```systemverilog
  input wire [7:0]  s_axis_tdata,
  input wire        s_axis_tvalid,
  input wire [15:0] prescale
);

    .clk(clk), .rst(rst),
    .s_axis_tdata(s_axis_tdata), .s_axis_tvalid(s_axis_tvalid), .s_axis_tready(s_axis_tready),
    .txd(txd), .busy(busy),
    .prescale(prescale)
  );

  reg init = 1'b1;
  always @(posedge clk) init <= 1'b0;

  // Reset at the start: every testbench, baseline and gold resets first, and
  // the RTL's register initialisers equal its reset values.
  always @(*) if (init) assume(rst);

  // prescale in 1..4: keeps a bit period at 8..32 clocks so frames fit the
  // bound. A bound on the search, not a spec rule (README: prescale =
  // Fclk / (baud * 8), any 16-bit value); items that need a large prescale
  // (T2: 16'hFFFF) are out of bound by construction.
  always @(*) assume(prescale >= 16'd1 && prescale <= 16'd4);

  // input set for a baud rate; changing it mid-frame is not legal stimulus.
  always @(posedge clk) if (!init && $past(busy)) assume(prescale == $past(prescale));

  // s2.8.2: TVALID is driven low during reset.

  // s2.2.1: once TVALID is asserted it stays asserted, and TDATA stays stable,
  // until the handshake (TVALID && TREADY). A reset ends the obligation.
  always @(posedge clk)
    if (!init && !rst && !$past(rst) && $past(s_axis_tvalid && !s_axis_tready))
```

// Transmit at the minimum prescale (16'd1): every data bit lasts 8 clocks and
// the bits sampled at the data-bit boundaries form 8'h96.
module cov_ITEM (
  input logic        clk,
  input logic        rst,
  input logic [15:0] prescale,
  input logic [18:0] prescale_reg,
  input logic [3:0]  bit_cnt,
  input logic        txd,
  input logic        s_axis_tvalid
);

  localparam logic [15:0] PS     = 16'd1;
  localparam logic [4:0]  PERIOD = 5'd7;  // non-boundary clocks per bit

  reg [7:0] shift;
  reg       active;
  reg       done;
  reg       ok;
  reg [4:0] cyc;

  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst) begin
      shift  <= 8'h00;
      active <= 1'b0;
      done   <= 1'b0;
      ok     <= 1'b0;
      cyc    <= 5'd0;
    end else begin
      done <= 1'b0;
      if (prescale_reg == 19'd0) begin
        cyc <= 5'd0;
      end else if (cyc != 5'd31) begin
        cyc <= cyc + 5'd1;

      if (prescale_reg == 19'd0 && bit_cnt == 4'd0 && s_axis_tvalid) begin
        active <= (prescale == PS);
        shift  <= 8'h00;
        ok     <= 1'b1;
      end else if (active && prescale_reg == 19'd0 && bit_cnt != 4'd0 && bit_cnt <= 4'd8) begin

        if (cyc != PERIOD) begin
          ok <= 1'b0;
        end
        if (bit_cnt == 4'd1) begin
          done   <= 1'b1;
          active <= 1'b0;
        end

      if (prescale != PS) begin
        active <= 1'b0;
      end
